style.vernacular: Middle Belt river town on the Benue with a north bank and a south bank joined by the 1932 rail bridge and the 1978 dual-carriage road bridge. Ordinary buildings are 1-3 storey cement-block structures in cream, ochre or pale-green painted render under long-span coloured corrugated metal roofs, often with plain concrete verandas and louvred windows; walls are weathered by the heavy rains and red laterite dust. Traditional Tiv compounds (round mud-render huts under thatch) survive at the fringes. Large government and institutional compounds from the 1960s-80s are modernist concrete blocks. Colours here are typical Middle Belt Nigerian palettes, not individually sourced.
style.ornament: Plain verandas with concrete column rows and louvred windows; breeze-block screens and painted perimeter walls with gate piers; murals and political/commercial signboards on market walls; Tiv a'nger black-and-white stripe pattern occasionally appears in painted bands (cloth pattern only, no building evidence).

sources.what: Benue River town, north bank/south bank split, 1932 rail bridge and 1978 dual carriage bridge, hot humid savanna climate, rainfall ~1,217 mm, institutions named
